theme.name: Guild Ledger
theme.description: A premium campaign-ledger workspace with ink navy and slate structure, warm parchment/cream text, antique brass for brand and primary actions, restrained ledger blue for information/focus, and wine-seal red only for small brand or semantic accents.

architecture.principle: One shared product brain, isolated presentation layers.
architecture.backend: API, persistence, authentication, sync, campaign/character data and server-side business logic.
architecture.frontendCore: API client, auth, shared state, routing and data hooks. Device-independent.
architecture.features: Campaigns, characters, quests, combat, dice, NPCs, maps and Rook logic. Device-independent where possible.

layouts.desktop: Wide workspace, permanent navigation, multi-panel tools when space allows.
layouts.tablet: Touch-first layout with portrait/landscape adaptations and reduced navigation footprint.
layouts.mobile: Bottom/compact navigation, one primary task at a time, sheets/drawers instead of desktop floating windows.

cssRules: Global CSS may define reset, typography, design tokens, accessibility and true app-shell foundations only.
Feature/page styling must be imported by that feature or layout rather than App.js.
Prefer CSS Modules or otherwise tightly scoped selectors for new layout work.
Do not use global !important layers to recolour or resize unrelated screens.
Do not reintroduce neon-pink, broad Rookie-red, Sunset/Twilight purple, glow-heavy chrome, route-wide parchment/leather skins, or competing global visual systems.
A theme change must not alter workspace geometry, rail width, card columns or page flow.
Desktop, tablet and mobile may render different presentation components while sharing the same hooks, data and actions.
productRules: Prep builds the campaign library; Live Play uses and updates it.
Multiple quests may be active; a focused/current quest is a convenience only.
Rook suggests; the GM decides. Rook must not silently change canon or state.
Create Character and Import Character are the only supported character-entry paths.
Failed refreshes must preserve last-known-good data and must never masquerade as valid empty data or successful actions.
